look_here_first: LOOK HERE FIRST: Check for a persistent woody shrub with many short gray-green wedge-shaped leaves, commonly ending in three short rounded teeth. Confirm gray-brown woody stems and, when present, upright sprays of tiny heads. Three tips alone are not proof: compare the shrub habit and leaf proportions.
taxonomy_notes: POWO accepts Artemisia tridentata at species rank and recognizes multiple subspecies. The source pool is species-level. Do not assign a subspecies from a Utah photograph or create synonym duplicates.

morphology_keys.habit: Aromatic, gray-haired, woody shrub typically 0.4–2 m tall, sometimes larger; substantial older trunks and branches with exfoliating gray bark; not rhizomatous.
morphology_keys.leaves_attachment: Persistent small gray-green leaves on shoots, typically wedge-shaped, 0.5–3.5 cm long and narrow, commonly shallowly three-lobed at tip with rounded lobes; some leaves may be entire.
morphology_keys.flower_reproductive: Tiny discoid heads in upright, branching panicle-like clusters; narrow involucres around 1.5–4 mm long, with woolly phyllaries; no showy rays.
morphology_keys.fruit_seed: Small dry one-seeded cypselae around 1–2 mm; inspect under magnification.
morphology_keys.stem_bud: Woody gray-brown branches, gray bark peeling in strips; gray-hairy vegetative growth.

confused_with: Artemisia ludoviciana (rhizomatous, upright perennial herb with much larger and more variable leaves, rather than a persistent woody shrub)
Artemisia tripartita (leaves more deeply three-lobed with narrow acute lobes; shrub often root-sprouting)
Artemisia arbuscula (much smaller low sagebrush; use mature shrub habit and heads)
comparisons.key_distinctions: Combine persistent woody shrub habit with short, gray-green wedge-shaped leaves bearing three shallow rounded terminal lobes. In A. tripartita lobes are proportionally deeper; A. ludoviciana is a rhizomatous herb.
